น่าน.title_original: Care gaps hold back Thai women’s employment
น่าน.summary_original:
Thailand’s strong gains in girls’ education and maternal health have yet to translate into equal economic opportunities, political leadership or personal safety for women, according to the Thailand Country Gender Equality Profile 2026 launched by the United Nations at the Sustainability Expo 2026 (SX2026) in Bangkok.

Produced jointly by the UN in Thailand, UN Women and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in partnership with the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security (MSDHS), the report highlights a stark disconnect between educational attainment and workforce participation. While women outpace men in tertiary education enrollment at 51.6 per cent compared to 38.6 per cent, female labour force participation remains stagnant at 58.9 per cent, lagging well behind men’s 74.7 per cent.

Unpaid care work is identified as the primary barrier holding women back. Among working-age women outside the labour market, 87.3 per cent cite unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities as the reason, compared with just 16.3 per cent of men. Gaps in affordable childcare for children under three and insufficient elder care services continue to constrain women’s career choices as Thailand transitions into a super-aged society.

“Thailand’s achievements in girls’ education and women’s health show what sustained investment in public services can deliver,” said UN Resident Coordinator Michaela Friberg-Storey. “The next step is to ensure that these gains translate into equal opportunities to earn a living, lead and live free from violence. That requires tackling the barriers women face at home, at work and in public life.”

Gender-based violence and underrepresentation in decision-making also remain pressing concerns. The report notes that 32.9 per cent of ever-partnered women aged 15–49 have experienced physical or sexual intimate partner violence in their lifetime, with 14.3 per cent experiencing it within the past year. Meanwhile, following the February 2026 elections, women hold 19.8 per cent of seats in the House of Representatives and 22.5 per cent in the Senate—still short of national representation targets.

United Nations Assistant Secretary-General and UN Women Deputy Executive Director Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda stressed that data-driven action is essential to reach marginalised groups, including rural women, migrant workers, LGBTQI+ individuals and women with disabilities. “This profile provides a shared evidence base for action. By using its findings to guide policies, budgets and services, we can address persistent inequalities and ensure that progress reaches women and girls who face the greatest barriers,” she said.

During a panel discussion on women’s economic empowerment moderated by UN Women Goodwill Ambassador Cindy Sirinya Bishop, representatives from the public and private sectors outlined concrete steps to address the care burden and expand opportunities.

Representing the MSDHS’s Department of Women’s Affairs and Family Development, specialist Urupin Singhanoi said the ministry is advancing gender-responsive budgeting alongside a proposed family leave policy that would allow men to take leave for caregiving duties. The ministry is also rolling out professional care training programmes and a community-based “one tambon, one caregiver” initiative to support families with elderly dependents.

From the private sector, CLP Axtra Plx. Chief Sustainability and Corporate Communications Officer Siriporn Dechsingha noted that women own 51 per cent of the retailer’s supplier network, with a target to reach 60 per cent. To help female farmers and entrepreneurs overcome travel and caregiving constraints, the company launched an online sourcing portal and is expanding regional agricultural learning centres across four regions. Internally, CP Axtra provides lactation rooms across its Makro and Lotus’s branches and has opened traditionally male-dominated roles, such as delivery fleet management, to women, who now make up 58 per cent of its executive team.

Meanwhile, Office of Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion (OSMEP) Assistant Director-General Wittawat Lamsam said the agency has established a formal national definition for women-owned enterprises in collaboration with UN Women. The standardised classification will enable financial institutions and state agencies to better track data and direct targeted credit and market access programmes to female entrepreneurs under Thailand’s upcoming five-year SME master plan.

น่าน.title: Malaysian Student Develops AI Tool to Help Detect Online Scams
น่าน.summary:
KUALA LUMPUR, Malaysia — A final-year student at Universiti Malaya has developed a web application designed to help users identify potential online scams and AI-generated content after becoming a victim of an AI-powered scam himself.
Min Han, who studies Computer Systems and Networks at the Faculty of Computer Science and Information Technology, is developing a platform called TruthLens to help people recognise early warning signs of scams, particularly those involving artificial intelligence (AI).

“Even though I’m studying cybersecurity, I still fell for it,” he said.
“That made me ask: how can I help people who don’t have any cybersecurity knowledge avoid these traps and the losses they can cause?”
Min Han said he was also concerned about the financial impact of AI-enabled fraud in Malaysia, citing an estimate that such scams caused RM2.7 billion in losses in 2025. The figure was not independently verified in his presentation.
Combining AI Detection with Scam Awareness
TruthLens is designed to analyse images for potential signs of AI generation and provide users with information that could help them assess whether the content is suspicious.

The application combines several detection methods, including AI detection models, pixel-level analysis and SynthID watermark detection, a technology used to identify certain AI-generated content.
During a demonstration, Min Han uploaded an image to the platform to show how the system examines visual content and presents its findings.

The application uses Google’s Gemini AI to translate technical detection results into explanations that are easier for users without cybersecurity expertise to understand.
Gemini also helps identify additional warning signs that could suggest an image may be used in a scam.

However, AI detection tools have limitations, and their findings do not necessarily establish whether an image is authentic or being used for fraudulent purposes.
Min Han said the objective of TruthLens extends beyond identifying potentially manipulated content. He hopes the platform will help users develop the knowledge needed to recognise suspicious material independently.
Min Han said access to Google’s Gemini and Google Cloud technologies has enabled him to experiment with different approaches to AI detection while developing his technical skills.

“It has also helped me understand what I need for my future career.”
The development of TruthLens comes amid growing concerns about the use of AI-generated images and other synthetic content in online fraud, which can make it more difficult for internet users to distinguish genuine material from potentially deceptive content.
Min Han’s project focuses on making technical detection methods more accessible to the public while encouraging users to assess online content critically.

The presentation did not specify when TruthLens would become publicly available or provide independent testing results on the platform’s detection accuracy.
For now, the project illustrates how AI tools are being applied by university students to address online safety challenges, while highlighting the importance of public awareness alongside technological solutions.

​”What is good, Boom says it’s good” was the advertising catchphrase of the soap brand, which has become a mantra that many Thais, who are exposed to the phrase over the two decades, would instantly recognise. And yet, the soap company has now terminated her contract.

When Boom’s reputation was supposedly “impeccable,” these very fair-weather friends and admirers relished taking selfies with Boom and praising her. Now it’s the opposite. When she was popular, fair-weather friends got instant social media visibility when posting with Boom. Now that she’s infamous, these very people instead get more social media attention by summarily denouncing Boom as a fake “good person.”
​How convenient…
​Guilty until proven innocent, not innocent until proven guilty, is many Thai people’s understanding of justice. They are quick to judge, and quick to believe or be scammed — but even quicker to ditch her, now that she is being detained and branded as arguably the biggest Thai scammer of the decade.
​The problematic notion of “good people” that are too good to be true is prevalent in Thailand. Many Thais love idealised or vilified characterisations — it’s either simplistic white or black. Many Thais are fond of public figures who are too good to be true. Boom is not the only such idol.

น่าน.summary_original:
Everything happened so abruptly that when I took a bus on Sukhumvit Road earlier this week, the soap ads inside the bus—where “Boom” Panadda Wongphudee is, or was, the brand ambassador for 24 long years—were still lit bright, while Boom herself is being detained after being accused of siphoning a massive amount of public donations made to her foundation, supposedly meant for helping needy people, for personal indulgence instead.

​”What is good, Boom says it’s good” was the advertising catchphrase of the soap brand, which has become a mantra that many Thais, who are exposed to the phrase over the two decades, would instantly recognise. And yet, the soap company has now terminated her contract.

​The fair-weather friends readily ditch her, even though the justice process has just begun. When Boom’s reputation was supposedly “impeccable,” these very fair-weather friends and admirers relished taking selfies with Boom and praising her. Now it’s the opposite. When she was popular, fair-weather friends got instant social media visibility when posting with Boom. Now that she’s infamous, these very people instead get more social media attention by summarily denouncing Boom as a fake “good person.”

​How convenient…

​Guilty until proven innocent, not innocent until proven guilty, is many Thai people’s understanding of justice. They are quick to judge, and quick to believe or be scammed — but even quicker to ditch her, now that she is being detained and branded as arguably the biggest Thai scammer of the decade.

​The problematic notion of “good people” that are too good to be true is prevalent in Thailand. Many Thais love idealised or vilified characterisations — it’s either simplistic white or black. Many Thais are fond of public figures who are too good to be true. Boom is not the only such idol.

​People can be too trusting. Prone to fairy tales. No wonder scam victims are plentiful in Thailand.

According to findings released by Thailand’s Economic Crime Suppression Division (ECD) this month regarding Boom’s “Do Good” Foundation (Ongkorn Thamdee), police have not specified the exact number of unique individuals who donated, as many people contributed multiple times. However, investigators tracked over 3.2 million separate donation transfers across three bank accounts totaling over 815 million baht.

The amount allegedly siphoned, according to investigators, is 527 million baht, or approximately 65 per cent of the total donations, diverted for personal benefit rather than charitable work.

​Police reported that the 527 million baht was channelled into 12 categories of non-charitable expenditures. These included 99 million baht transferred directly to her husband, Atip “Got” Anantawan; 36 million baht transferred to foundation committee members; 24 million baht invested in mutual funds; 19 million baht spent on personal credit card bills; and 18 million baht paid to contractors for building a pool villa in Phuket (with additional transfers linked to construction projects in Pathum Thani). Also, 10 million baht spent on life insurance and 4.6 million baht transferred to Panadda’s father.

Then there was 2.7 million baht spent on luxury handbags and jewelry, which was withdrawn from mutual fund accounts.

The bottom line: Only about 280 million baht of the total funds collected was found to have actually been used for legitimate foundation activities.

Khaosod English reports on Wednesday that police revealed approximately 90 per cent of the first batch of 32 designer handbags seized in the investigation appear to be counterfeit, pending official authentication.

On Wednesday, investigators searched two more condominiums registered in Panadda’s name, seizing another 12 designer handbags, 53 pieces of jewellery, 11 scarves, and four items of clothing. Police are now tracing the origins of the luxury goods and the money used to purchase them, while questioning people linked to the foundation’s financial transactions.

​The shockwave through the whole “Do Good” industry is palpable, with the authorities now looking into a dozen other well-known foundations for possible misuse of public donations.

​Henceforth, there needs to be more transparency and accountability. Details of donations made, and how much and how it was spent, should be posted online for all to examine and independently reviewed by a third-party auditor on a monthly basis.
​
Temple donations should also be better regulated, as there are, according to official statistics from the National Office of Buddhism (ONAB), over 44,000 active, registered Buddhist temples, or wat, across the country. Misuse and wasteful use of resources by temples should also be tackled, with fewer concrete structures and more hospices, shelters for the poor, orphans, and elderly, and schools preferred.

​In the end, whatever you think about Boom, she should be regarded as innocent until proven guilty. I am not a fan of Boom and had never donated to her “Do Good” Foundation.

Nevertheless, if Thai society learned a thing or two from this case, then perhaps not all the donated money went to waste — to real or counterfeit luxury bags, and more.

น่าน.title: Thailand’s Online Shopping Rules Face Major Changes
น่าน.summary:
BANGKOK – Thailand’s Cabinet approved a sweeping expansion of import duties on overseas online shopping purchases Tuesday, Nov. 10, ending tariff discounts for cross-border parcels arriving via express couriers and international postal services. Proposed by the Ministry of Finance, the measure applies standard customs classifications—capped at 30%—to protect Thai retailers from low-priced foreign competition.

The policy will raise checkout prices for millions of Thai shoppers ordering from foreign e-commerce platforms starting in 2027. Customs officials project the overhaul will generate 6.3 billion baht in extra annual duty revenue while curbing false value declarations on small shipments.

• Category-Based Rates: Import duties follow standard customs tariff schedules up to a 30% ceiling rather than a universal flat tax.

• Total Cost Stacking: Duties apply to the combined product price, shipping and insurance cost, with Thailand’s 7% value-added tax added on top.

The 30% figure is a legal ceiling, not a flat fee on every package. Under rules outlined by the Customs Department, each item is taxed by its Harmonized System tariff code. Many goods carry rates between 5% and 20%, though popular categories face steep hikes. Imitation jewelry and communications gear jump from zero to 30%, while headphones and fitness gear rise from 10% to 30%. Women’s handbags climb from 20% to 30%, and clothing stays at 30%.

Those percentages hit more than the sticker price. Customs assessors calculate duties using Cost, Insurance and Freight (CIF) value, folding shipping charges into the taxable base. Thailand’s 7% value-added tax then applies to the combined sum of product price, delivery fee and duty. A 1,000-baht pair of wireless earbuds with 100 baht in shipping draws a 330-baht duty at 30%, pushing 7% VAT to 100 baht and the final bill to 1,530 baht.

Tuesday’s decision caps a two-year crackdown on cross-border e-commerce loopholes. For years, overseas parcels worth under 1,500 baht entered Thailand tax-free under a “de minimis” exemption. That system strained under regional factory-to-consumer apps. Inbound international parcels surged from 134.1 million in 2024 to 168.4 million in 2025, with volume projected to reach 241 million packages in 2026.

In January 2026, officials scrapped the 1,500-baht threshold and began collecting 7% VAT and discounted duties from the first baht. Customs Director-General Phantong Loykulnanta noted that reduced parcel rates still invited under-invoicing, while staffing shortages prevented officers from inspecting hundreds of millions of packets. Business groups, including the Federation of Thai Industries, urged the Cabinet to restore full tariffs, arguing domestic factories pay corporate taxes, wages and safety certification fees that foreign sellers avoid.

Buyers can avoid doorstep surprises by checking checkout terms before paying. Major regional marketplaces integrated with Thai customs systems collect duties and VAT upfront at payment, locking in the final landed price. Independent overseas websites often ship under Delivered Duty Unpaid terms, leaving express couriers to collect taxes plus brokerage fees upon delivery.

น่าน.title: Italy seal dominant win over France, Kane sets England appearance record
น่าน.summary:
MILAN, Nov 12 : Italy produced a dominant performance to beat France 3-1 in the Nations League on Thursday, while Harry Kane celebrated his record 126th cap for England with a match-winning penalty as England beat Croatia 2-1 to qualify for the last eight.

Michael Olise gave France the lead in Milan, but a double from Francesco Pio Esposito and one from Davide Frattesi secured a deserved win for the Italians.

Kane, who surpassed Peter Shilton's tally of 125 appearances, stepped up in the 64th minute to put England ahead at Wembley Stadium after the hosts had conceded a sloppy equaliser five minutes earlier.

Italy, France and Belgium will battle it out next Tuesday for two quarter-final spots, with Roberto Mancini's side level at the top of League A Group 1 with France on 10 points.

Plenty of soul-searching followed Italy's failure to qualify for the 2026 World Cup but Mancini's side showed they are more than capable of competing with the best.

Flooding the midfield, Italy's smart and cohesive work proved too much for their opponents.

Michael Olise gave France an early lead after an error from Gianluigi Donnarumma, but excellent work from Nicolo Cambiaghi set up Francesco Pio Esposito for the equaliser in the 26th minute.

Bradley Barcola thudded the post before halftime, but Italy were far more comfortable than Zinedine Zidane's side, who were without Real Madrid duo Kylian Mbappe and Aurelien Tchouameni through injury.

For a second time Cambiaghi flew past Malo Gusto to win a penalty, but Sebastiano Esposito could not convert on the hour mark. Three minutes later Davide Frattesi burst onto a Federico Dimarco cross to give the Italians the lead.

When Antonio Vergara won a second Italy penalty, Pio Esposito made no mistake from the spot in the 75th minute.

The Italian side braced themselves for a late onslaught, but to the delight of the home crowd, found they were able to fend off France's attacks with ease.

Belgium lie one point behind Italy and France after a 2-1 win over Turkey, who fell to a fifth straight defeat and will be relegated to League B.

Morgan Rogers opened the scoring for England in the 24th minute, while Petar Sucic equalised for Croatia in the 59th minute as Thomas Tuchel's side struggled to push on.

Parity lasted all of five minutes after Jarrell Quansah was fouled in the Croatian box, handing England captain Kane the chance to mark his milestone with a 92nd international goal. The freshly crowned Ballon d'Or winner barely broke stride on his way to celebrate.

World champions Spain won 2-0 away against Czechia to keep themselves top of Group 3 in League A, three points ahead of England before they meet on Sunday. Both sides are already qualified for the knockout stages.

Alex Baena scored a penalty in the 39th minute after Lukas Ambros handled the ball in his box. Czechia put Spain under pressure as the second half progressed, and hit the woodwork through Adam Hlozek.

The Czech fightback was curtailed by Ladislav Krejci's 72nd-minute red card for a last-man challenge, and in stoppage time Marc Pubill added a second.

In League C, Albania and Belarus both sealed 2-0 wins over Finland and San Marino respectively. Armenia and Cyprus drew 1-1, which combined with Montenegro's 2-1 victory over Latvia, means the Balkan side have secured top spot in their group.

น่าน.title: Advantech จับมือ Qonnect ดัน AI ฝีมือไทยสู่ตลาดโลก ชู Co-Creation พัฒนา AI-Powered PHM ตอบโจทย์โรงงานอุตสาหกรรม
น่าน.summary:
ท่ามกลางการแข่งขันของภาคการผลิตที่ต้องบริหารต้นทุน รักษาประสิทธิภาพการผลิต และลดความเสี่ยงจากเครื่องจักรหยุดทำงานโดยไม่คาดคิด การนำ AI มาใช้ให้เกิดผลจริงในโรงงานจึงเป็นโจทย์สำคัญ ขณะเดียวกันความร่วมมือกับพันธมิตรระดับโลกยังเปิดโอกาสให้บริษัทเทคโนโลยีไทยนำความเชี่ยวชาญของตนเองไปเติบโตในตลาดต่างประเทศ
บริษัท แอดวานซ์เทค คอร์ปอเรชั่น (ประเทศไทย) จำกัด (Advantech Corporation (Thailand) Co., Ltd.) ผู้นำระดับโลกด้านโซลูชัน Edge AI, Industrial IoT และคอมพิวเตอร์เกรดอุตสาหกรรม ร่วมมือกับ Qonnect บริษัทสตาร์ทอัพด้านเทคโนโลยีที่ก่อตั้งในปี 2020 ภายใต้บริษัท บีไอไอซี จำกัด (BIIC Co., Ltd.) ในเครือเอสซีจี ซึ่งพัฒนาโซลูชัน IIoT, AI และแพลตฟอร์มดิจิทัล เพื่อยกระดับประสิทธิภาพและขับเคลื่อนการเปลี่ยนผ่านสู่ดิจิทัลของโรงงานอุตสาหกรรม

(ซ้ายสุด) คุณ Scott Sun, Manager of Industrial Connectivity & Wireless Group และ (ขวาสุด) คุณ Elvin Ng, Managing Director of South Asia Pacific Region, Advantech
หัวใจของความร่วมมือคือ Co-Creation หรือการร่วมสร้างนวัตกรรม โดยผสานโครงสร้างพื้นฐานเทคโนโลยีอุตสาหกรรมของ Advantech กับความเชี่ยวชาญด้าน AI และความเข้าใจปัญหาหน้างานของ Qonnect เพื่อพัฒนาโซลูชันที่ใช้งานได้จริง พร้อมวางรากฐานการเติบโตร่วมกันในตลาดโลก
จากประสบการณ์วิศวกร SCG สู่การร่วมพัฒนาเทคโนโลยี

เปิดเผยว่า จุดเริ่มต้นความร่วมมือกับ Advantech เกิดจากประสบการณ์ทำงานเป็นวิศวกรใน SCG เมื่อกว่า 10 ปีก่อน ซึ่งได้ใช้อุปกรณ์ Remote I/O และ Industrial PC ของ Advantech ในการพัฒนาระบบเครื่องจักร ต่อมาเมื่อเริ่มพัฒนา Vibration Analysis Platform และโซลูชัน Prognostics and Health Management (PHM) สำหรับโรงงานในเครือ SCG ที่มีมากกว่า 300 แห่ง โจทย์สำคัญคือทำให้การวิเคราะห์สภาพเครื่องจักรเข้าถึงได้ง่ายขึ้น โดยไม่ต้องพึ่งผู้เชี่ยวชาญเฉพาะทางประจำทุกโรงงาน
“โจทย์คือทำอย่างไรให้การทำ Vibration Analysis ง่ายขึ้น โดยลดการพึ่งพา Vibration Specialist ลง เพราะ SCG มีบริษัทในเครือ 300 กว่าโรงงาน จึงเป็นไปไม่ได้ที่จะจ้าง Specialist ประจำทุกโรง เพราะค่าตัวแพงมาก เราเลยพัฒนาซอฟต์แวร์ที่ใคร ๆ ก็วิเคราะห์การสั่นสะเทือนได้” คุณพชรกล่าว
หลังจากทดลองเซนเซอร์หลายทางเลือก Qonnect พบว่า WISE-2410 หรือ Wireless Vibration Sensor ของ Advantech สามารถทำงานร่วมกับแพลตฟอร์มได้ จึงเริ่มหารือและทดสอบ Proof of Concept (POC) ร่วมกัน ทั้งในและนอกเครือ SCG ก่อนต่อยอดเป็นความร่วมมือทางธุรกิจ โดยคุณพชรเล่าว่า “ระบบซอฟต์แวร์ไทยสามารถนำมาทำงานร่วมกับฮาร์ดแวร์มาตรฐานระดับโลกได้อย่างราบรื่น”
ความสำคัญของเทคโนโลยีดังกล่าวเห็นได้จากปัญหา Unplanned Downtime หรือการหยุดเครื่องจักรโดยไม่ได้วางแผน คุณพชรยกตัวอย่างโรงงานผลิตแก้วพลาสติกแห่งหนึ่งในจังหวัดระยองที่มีเครื่องฉีดพลาสติกราว 100-200 เครื่อง และมีชั่วโมงหยุดทำงานของเครื่องจักรสะสมรวมประมาณ 100,000 ชั่วโมงต่อปี
“จริง ๆ ตัวเลขมูลค่าความเสียหายอย่างชัดเจนอาจจะบอกไม่ได้ แต่ตัวเลขที่ผมมี จากการไปสัมภาษณ์โรงงานของลูกค้า ซึ่งเป็นโรงงานผลิตแก้วพลาสติกอยู่ที่ระยอง มี Downtime ปีหนึ่ง 100,000 ชั่วโมง ซึ่งเยอะมาก ๆ”
“ลองจินตนาการว่าแก้วน้ำ 1 ใบ สมมุติใบละ 2 บาท ปีหนึ่ง 100,000 ชั่วโมงจะเสียหายไปประมาณเท่าไหร่”
AI-Powered PHM: จากข้อมูลสั่นสะเทือนสู่การตัดสินใจเชิงรุก
โซลูชัน AI-Powered PHM ที่ทั้งสองบริษัทร่วมพัฒนาประกอบด้วย WISE-2410 Wireless Vibration Sensor ของ Advantech และ AI Predictive Maintenance Platform ของ Qonnect ระบบนำข้อมูลเครื่องจักรมาวิเคราะห์ด้วย Machine Learning เพื่อเรียนรู้รูปแบบการทำงานเฉพาะของแต่ละเครื่อง โดยคุณพชรระบุว่าใช้เวลาฝึกแบบจำลองราว 30-90 วันตามกรณีใช้งาน และจากประสบการณ์ของบริษัท สามารถแจ้งเตือนแนวโน้ม Emergency Breakdown ได้ล่วงหน้าเฉลี่ยประมาณสองสัปดาห์

3 D Analysis Dashboard

น่าน.title: พานาโซนิค ปลุกพลังพนักงาน สานต่อกิจกรรมวิ่งการกุศล ส่งเสริมสุขภาพ ช่วยเหลือสังคมอย่างยั่งยืน
น่าน.summary:
พานาโซนิค ปลุกพลังพนักงาน สานต่อกิจกรรมวิ่งการกุศล ส่งเสริมสุขภาพ สร้างพื้นที่สีเขียว ช่วยเหลือสังคมอย่างยั่งยืน
เมื่อวันที่ 13 พฤศจิกายน กลุ่มบริษัทพานาโซนิคในประเทศไทย เดินหน้าสานต่อนโยบายการมีส่วนร่วมพัฒนาสังคมสู่ความยั่งยืน จัดกิจกรรมวิ่งการกุศล “Panasonic Hero Run: Green Impact for Charity 2026” ขึ้น ณ สถานีกลางกรุงเทพอภิวัฒน์ โดยได้รับเกียรติจาก มร.ฮิเดคาสึ อิโตะ ซีอีโอ กลุ่มบริษัทพานาโซนิคในประเทศไทย พร้อมด้วยคณะผู้บริหาร พนักงาน ครอบครัว คู่ค้าธุรกิจ และนักเรียนทุนพานาโซนิค รวมกว่า 900 คน เข้าร่วมแสดงพลังแห่งการให้และความร่วมมือร่วมใจกันอย่างคับคั่ง
กิจกรรมในครั้งนี้จัดขึ้นภายใต้แนวคิด “รวมพลังแห่งการให้” มุ่งเน้นส่งเสริมให้ทุกคนตระหนักถึงความสำคัญของการดูแลสุขภาพ สังคม และสิ่งแวดล้อมไปพร้อมกัน โดยระยะทางวิ่งทุก ๆ 10 กม.ของทุกคนจะถูกแปลเปลี่ยนเป็นต้นไม้ 1 ต้น เพื่อปลูกป่าชายเลน ที่จังหวัดสมุทรสงคราม นอกจากนี้ ทุกคนยังได้มีส่วนร่วมในการบริจาคเงินสมทบทุนเพื่อช่วยเหลือสนับสนุนในการจัดหาอุปกรณ์ทางการแพทย์ที่จำเป็น ให้แก่ โรงพยาบาลน่าน จังหวัดน่าน ที่ได้รับผลกระทบจากอุทกภัยเพื่อฟื้นฟูและเสริมศักยภาพการให้บริการด้านสุขภาพแก่ประชาชน อย่างทั่วถึงและเท่าเทียม โดยได้รับเกียรติจาก นายแพทย์สุพจน์ ช่างเอกวงศ์ รองผู้อำนวยการด้านการแพทย์ โรงพยาบาลน่าน เป็นตัวแทนรับมอบ

สำหรับกิจกรรม “Panasonic Hero Run: Green Impact for Charity 2026” จัดขึ้นภายใต้โครงการ “พานาโซนิค แคร์ (Panasonic Cares)” ซึ่งดำเนินการต่อเนื่องเข้าสู่ปีที่ 6 มุ่งมั่นดำเนินกิจกรรมที่สอดคล้องกับเป้าหมายการพัฒนาที่ยั่งยืน (Sustainable Development Goals: SDGs) ในหลายมิติ ทั้งยังสอดรับกับภารกิจด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมระยะยาวของพานาโซนิค กรุ๊ป ทั่วโลก คือ “Panasonic Green Impact” ภารกิจด้านสิ่งแวดล้อมระดับโลกของพานาโซนิคกรุ๊ป ที่มุ่งสร้างผลลัพธ์เชิงบวกต่อโลกอย่างเป็นรูปธรรม โดยพานาโซนิคในประเทศไทยได้ริเริ่มแนวคิด “วิ่งเพื่อปลูกต้นไม้” โดยทุก ๆ 10 กิโลเมตรของระยะทางวิ่งโดยรวมของพนักงานทุกคน จะเท่ากับการปลูกต้นไม้ 1 ต้น มาใช้เป็นแนวคิดหลักเพื่อคืนพื้นที่สีเขียวให้ชุมชน ซึ่งตลอดระยะเวลาที่ผ่านมาได้ปลูกต้นไม้คืนสู่ธรรมชาติแล้วกว่า 3,117 ต้น ในจังหวัดขอนแก่น (570 ต้น) จังหวัดพระนครศรีอยุธยา (1,325 ต้น) และจังหวัดชลบุรี (1,222 ต้น)
ความพิเศษของกิจกรรมในปีนี้ พานาโซนิคในประเทศไทย ได้ชวนพนักงานมาร่วมวิ่งเพื่อสะสมระยะทาง โดยแบ่งกิจกรรมออกเป็น 2 รูปแบบ ได้แก่ การวิ่งแบบ Virtual Run โดยเก็บระยะวิ่งกันในช่วงเดือนตุลาคมที่ผ่านมา และการวิ่งในสนามจริง ซึ่งสามารถสะสมระยะทางรวมทั้งหมดได้กว่า 7,896 กิโลเมตร รวมกับการแยกขวดพลาสติก และกระป๋องจากกิจกรรม Let’s Grow แยก-ชั่ง-ปลูก รวมเปลี่ยนเป็นต้นไม้ทั้งหมด 1,013 ต้น เพื่อเตรียมปลูกในป่าชายเลน จ.สมุทรสงคราม พร้อมมอบเหรียญ และของรางวัลพิเศษ ให้แก่นักวิ่งที่เข้าร่วมกิจกรรมทุกท่าน และที่สำคัญภายในงานยังให้ความสำคัญกับการจัดกิจกรรมอย่างเป็นมิตรต่อสิ่งแวดล้อม โดยใช้ ภาชนะที่ทำจากวัสดุรีไซเคิล ติดตั้ง จุดแยกขยะอย่างชัดเจน และมี เครื่องย่อยสลายเศษอาหาร เพื่อลดการสร้างขยะและมลพิษสู่สังคม กิจกรรมทั้งหมดนี้สะท้อนถึงความมุ่งมั่นของพานาโซนิคในการส่งต่อแนวคิด “วิ่งเพื่อสุขภาพ รักษ์โลกเพื่ออนาคต” เพื่อร่วมสร้างโลกที่ยั่งยืนไปด้วยกันอย่างแท้จริง

น่าน.summary_original:

9M 2026 total revenue hits THB 7,677mn, with net profit up 9.5% to THB 824mn
COM7 adds to earnings as Plan B advances iCare investment

Key Performance Highlights

  • Continued growth in 3Q 2026 performance: Total revenue of THB 2,601mn (+10.8% YoY) and net profit of THB 320mn (+10.2% YoY), bringing 9M 2026 total revenue to THB 7,677mn (+11.8% YoY) and net profit to THB 824mn (+9.5% YoY).
  • Improved profitability: 3Q 2026 gross profit margin was 36.0%, up from 31.6% last year, supported by growth in the sports marketing business, the revenue and cost structure of certain projects, and efficient cost management.
  • Driving growth through strategic investments: Began recognizing its share of profit from COM7 for the first quarter and is proceeding with the planned THB 860mn investment in iCare to capture growth in the mobile phone insurance market, driven by higher smartphone values and the installment trend.
  • Strong cash flow and financial discipline: Generated free cash flow of THB 2,676mn in 9M 2026, with D/E at 1.09x, while maintaining prudent liquidity management and monitoring financial covenants.

Operating Performance in 3Q 2026

Despite continued challenges in the economy and domestic purchasing power, Plan B sustained its growth in 3Q 2026, with total revenue of THB 2,601mn, up 10.8% YoY, driven by both core businesses. Operating profit rose 23.8% YoY to THB 578mn, outpacing revenue growth, reflecting improved business and cost efficiency, while EBITDA reached THB 1,229mn, up 9.0% YoY. Net profit was THB 320mn, up 10.2% YoY, despite a full quarter of finance costs from the COM7 investment, while its share of profit from COM7 has been recognized since September, marking the start of returns from this strategic investment.

The out-of-home media business continued to grow, with revenue of THB 1,950mn, up 2.5% YoY, and the utilization rate rising to 74.3% from 73.0% last year. All media segments grew, particularly static media and retail media such as department stores, supermarkets and convenience stores. The Company also continued to enhance the efficiency of its media portfolio management in strategic locations and extend partnerships with VGI and Hello Bangkok LED to strengthen its media network and expand long-term business opportunities.

The engagement marketing business was a key growth driver, with revenue of THB 615mn, up 49.4% YoY, led by the sports marketing business, which grew 79.3% YoY to THB 560mn on the successful management of marketing rights for the ASEAN Football Championship 2026 and the strong popularity of Rajadamnern World Series (RWS) among Thai and international audiences.

Strategic Developments and Recent Achievements

This marks another key step in expanding Plan B’s growth base through strategic investments. The Company recognized its share of profit from COM7 for the first quarter and is proceeding with its investment in iCare, a specialist in mobile phone insurance and electronic device protection. The Company sees growth opportunities from rising smartphone values, their essential role in daily life and the growing use of credit and installment purchases, which support long-term demand for device protection.

iCare’s key strength is its specialized expertise, combined with a strong customer base and distribution network within the COM7 ecosystem, enabling protection products to be offered alongside smartphone purchases and expanding its customer reach. It also opens opportunities for Plan B to extend media and marketing collaboration, creating new business opportunities and diversifying long-term profit sources.

Alongside its strategic investments, Plan B continued to expand Rajadamnern World Series (RWS) by enhancing the experience at Rajadamnern Stadium with Immersive Storytelling and taking the brand overseas through Road to RWS in Switzerland, which drew over 3,000 spectators, underscoring the potential of RWS to build a global audience and create new long-term growth opportunities.

Financial Position as of the end of 3Q 2026

Plan B maintained its financial strength, generating free cash flow of THB 2,676 million in 9M 2026 and holding cash and cash equivalents of THB 2,536 million at quarter-end. The debt-to-equity ratio (D/E) stood at 1.09x, while the Company remained focused on prudent liquidity and capital structure management, monitoring financial covenants, and maintaining its dividend policy of at least 50% of net profit to support long-term growth and investment opportunities, including iCare.

Strategic Outlook

For 4Q 2026, the Company expects support from seasonally higher advertising demand, as well as sports marketing, concerts and major year-end events. It will also recognize its share of profit from COM7 for a full quarter for the first time and proceed with its investment in iCare, expected to be completed by the end of 2026. The Company remains focused on sustaining growth momentum alongside improving operational efficiency, cost management and financial discipline to deliver quality growth and sustainable returns to shareholders.

น่าน.title: Bangkok Eases Pet Registration Rules to Aid City Renters
น่าน.summary:
BANGKOK — Bangkok Gov. Chadchart Sittipunt has ordered urgent revisions to the capital’s pet control ordinance after strict landlord consent rules stalled dog and cat registrations across the city. Announced Thursday at City Hall, the directive removes a major administrative roadblock for thousands of apartment tenants ahead of a Jan. 10, 2027 enforcement deadline.

Under existing rules enacted in 2024, renters must submit written permission from property owners before local district offices can microchip or register an animal. City health officials found that landlords routinely refuse to sign those forms to avoid liability, leaving tenants unable to comply with the law and risking fines of up to 25,000 baht.

• Bangkok Gov. Chadchart Sittipunt ordered the Health Department to revise pet registration rules so renters no longer need written landlord consent.

• City Hall previously delayed full enforcement of the B.E. 2567 pet control ordinance until Jan. 10, 2027, giving owners more time to comply.

The policy pivot reflects a sharp clash between public health goals and Bangkok’s dense housing reality. When the Bangkok Council postponed enforcement of the Ordinance on the Control of Keeping or Releasing Animals earlier this year, officials hoped a 12-month grace period would boost low registration numbers. Instead, mobile veterinary teams deploying across all 50 districts encountered a recurring bottleneck.

Many condominium buildings operate under strict juristic person bylaws that ban animals or quietly tolerate them without formal approval. Tenants feared eviction if they requested official signatures, while absentee landlords ignored paperwork requests altogether. Without registered microchips, the Bangkok Metropolitan Administration cannot track rabies vaccinations or curb stray populations, which remain a persistent public safety concern across urban neighborhoods. Chadchart instructed the Health Department to draft amendments decoupling municipal pet IDs from private lease disputes while keeping space-based animal quotas intact.

While regulators untangle residential red tape, private businesses across Bangkok are aggressively courting pet owners. Rising single-person households and delayed parenthood have transformed dogs and cats into primary family companions, fueling a domestic market valued at nearly 75 billion baht annually according to Krungsri Research.

Major retail developers now treat pet access as essential foot-traffic infrastructure rather than a novelty. Shopping complexes along Sukhumvit and Rama III host City Hall’s free mobile microchipping clinics alongside dedicated dog parks, stroller rentals and pet-friendly dining terraces. Residential developers are also adapting, launching new condominium towers with built-in grooming stations and rooftop exercise runs to attract young urban buyers willing to pay premium rents for legal pet-friendly leases.

น่าน.title: Malaysia says probing Megaspeed subsidiary over possible AI chip diversion
น่าน.summary:
SpeedMatrix, a Malaysian subsidiary of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia.

KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's trade ministry said on Friday (Nov 13) that it was working with customs to determine whether any chips brought into the country by SpeedMatrix, a local unit of Singapore-based cloud computing firm Megaspeed, were re-exported to other countries.

It came the day after Nvidia boss Jensen Huang resigned over an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang - a suspected Chinese spy and former top executive at Megaspeed.

Megaspeed is under scrutiny for allegedly steering Nvidia AI chips to China despite US export rules designed to slow the development of artificial intelligence technology by Beijing.

In a statement on Friday, Malaysia's Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI) said that Speedmatrix is a tenant at data centres in Malaysia and is allowed to bring AI chips into the country without a permit or license.

Currently, bringing AI chips into Malaysia does not require a permit or a licence. However, since July last year, anyone seeking to export, re-export, transship or transit "high-performance US AI chips" from or through Malaysia must obtain a permit.

Giving false information to customs authorities about such items is a "serious offence", said the ministry.

"MITI is therefore working with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department to determine whether any of the chips brought into Malaysia have since been reexported to other countries, and whether such reexports were carried out in accordance with the law," it said.

"Malaysia will carry out its own checks independently, in accordance with Malaysian law and based on the evidence available," it added.

The ministry said it "has never cleared" Megaspeed or its Malaysian affliate Speedmatrix.

Any verification visits carried out by the ministry at the data centre facilities were part of its regular monitoring of the sector, and should not be "taken to mean that a company has been cleared", it said.

MITI also said it was working closely with authorities in Singapore and the United States and is considering further measures to strengthen controls where necessary.

"While Malaysia does not enforce unilateral export controls imposed by other countries, all companies operating in Malaysia are expected to take such controls into account in their international business," it said.

The ministry called on companies not to misrepresent their dealings with government agencies, saying that stern action will be taken against those who break Malaysian law.

"Malaysia welcomes investment in data centres and technology, but will not allow itself to be used to get around export controls.

Singapore's Ministry of Home Affairs said on Thursday that physical servers had been purchased by companies under investigation and exported through Singapore to Malaysia without entering the Singapore market.

The police were investigating whether the servers had subsequently been routed from Malaysia to another destination, contrary to declarations made by the companies in Singapore.

The Nvidia scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off the company's market capitalisation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters.

ลำพูน.title: พบร่าง ‘ครูหนึ่ง’ เสียชีวิตอยู่ในรถบริเวณป่าลำพูน หลังหายจากบ้านที่ลำปาง 5 วัน
ลำพูน.summary:
พบร่าง ‘ครูหนึ่ง’ เสียชีวิตอยู่ในรถบริเวณป่า อ.ลี้ จ.ลำพูน หลังหายจากบ้านที่ลำปาง 5 วัน จากนั้นทางบ้านไม่สามารถติดต่อได้อีก
12 พ.ย. 69 – ความคืบหน้า น.ส.วิริยา พยอม หรือ “ครูหนึ่ง” อายุ 54 ปี ครูสอนอนุบาล โรงเรียนสบปราบ ออกจากบ้านที่ อ.เกาะคา จ.ลำปาง ตั้งแต่เวลา 06.47 น. วันที่ 7 พ.ย. จากนั้นทางบ้านไม่สามารถติดต่อได้อีก โดยได้ไปแจ้งความไว้ที่ สภ.เกาะคา
ล่าสุดวันนี้ เวลา 17.15 น. พนักงานสอบสวน สภ.ลี้ จ.ลำพูน ได้รับแจ้งจากชาวบ้าน ต.ลี้ อ.ลี้ ว่า เข้าไปกรีดยางแล้วพบรถเก๋งจอดอยู่ในป่าชุมชนบ้านปู ตั้งแต่ที่ 10 พ.ย. ที่ผ่านมา เจ้าหน้าที่ตำรวจพร้อมเจ้าหน้าที่กู้ภัยฯลี้ จึงเดินทางไปตรวจสอบ
ที่เกิดเหตุพบรถเก๋งนิสสัน อัลเมรา สีบรอนซ์ จอกซุกอยู่ในป่า ภายในรถพบร่างผู้เสียชีวิต สภาพขึ้นอืด จากการตรวจสอบภายในรถ พบผู้เสียชีวิตคือ น.ส.วิริยา หรือ “ครูหนึ่ง” ที่หายตัวไปก่อนหน้านี้
เจ้าหน้าที่ตรวจสอบกล้องวงจรปิดวันที่ 7 พ.ย. เวลา 08:05 น. พบครูหนึ่ง เข้ามาซื้อของในร้านชำในพื้นที่บ้านสันติสุข ต.เสริมซ้าย อ.เสริมงาม จ.ลำปาง ก่อนขับรถมุ่งหน้าต่อเข้าเขตพื้นที่ อ.ลี้ จ.ลำพูน
ด้านเจ้าหน้าที่และญาติ ขอความร่วมมือจากชาวบ้าน อ.ลี้ และ อ.บ้านโฮ่ง หรือพื้นที่ใกล้เคียง หากพบเห็นหรือทราบเบาะแสใด ๆ เกี่ยวกับ “ครูหนึ่ง” หรือรถเก๋งคันดังกล่าว กรุณาแจ้งเจ้าหน้าที่ตำรวจในพื้นที่

ตาก.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises US security concerns
ตาก.summary:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing raised U.S. national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO . She had been Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.
Huang’s resignation comes after Nvidia’s board gathered to discuss his future following revelations that he was having an affair with Alice Huang , a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of spying for China. The two aren’t related.
The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports.
Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, fell sharply at the opening bell Thursday.
Here’s the latest:
US lawmakers still expect a briefing with Jensen Huang
U.S. lawmakers say they still want a briefing from Jensen Huang despite his resignation so that he can answer questions about his interactions with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing.
They also want to ask about the company’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage as well as other topics.
Rep. Brian Mast, chairman of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, said the committee was in contact with Huang’s team as recently as Wednesday night about the interview. Lawmakers had made their initial request for the interview on Nov. 5. He also said that Huang would receive a subpoena, if necessary, to compel his appearance.
“They made their offer for what they would like to do, and we said, like in any negotiation, ‘no, this is what we’ll accept or your subpoena comes for the day after,’” Mast said.
Mast said Jensen has indicated a willingness to appear for the interview and that the committees involved in the inquiry wanted to see him “sooner rather than later.”
Nvidia shares fall after Huang’s resignation
Nvidia shares fell after the company announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO.
After tumbling at the open of trading, Nvidia shares were down 5.3% as of 10:30 a.m. EST Thursday.
The chipmaker became the face of the AI boom under Huang’s leadership. The shares set a record high last month after soaring an astounding 1,722% in four years. But Nvidia’s share price has dropped more than 30% since then, initially on concerns the enthusiasm over AI was overdone and this past week on worries about whether Huang would remain with the company.
The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and technology stocks were the biggest weights dragging down the benchmark index. Nvidia and several other tech companies have pricey stock values that tend to have more influence on the market’s direction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.7%.

ตาก.title_original: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after his affair raises US security concerns
ตาก.summary_original:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after his extramarital affair with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing raised U.S. national security concerns. The company named Colette Kress as interim CEO. She had been Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer.

Huang’s resignation comes after Nvidia’s board gathered to discuss his future following revelations that he was having an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed International suspected of spying for China. The two aren’t related.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. The Associated Press could not independently confirm those reports.

Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, fell sharply at the opening bell Thursday.

Here’s the latest:

US lawmakers still expect a briefing with Jensen Huang

U.S. lawmakers say they still want a briefing from Jensen Huang despite his resignation so that he can answer questions about his interactions with a Chinese businesswoman who reportedly was also acting as a spy for Beijing.

They also want to ask about the company’s security protocols against foreign adversary espionage as well as other topics.

Rep. Brian Mast, chairman of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, said the committee was in contact with Huang’s team as recently as Wednesday night about the interview. Lawmakers had made their initial request for the interview on Nov. 5. He also said that Huang would receive a subpoena, if necessary, to compel his appearance.

“They made their offer for what they would like to do, and we said, like in any negotiation, ‘no, this is what we’ll accept or your subpoena comes for the day after,’” Mast said.

Mast said Jensen has indicated a willingness to appear for the interview and that the committees involved in the inquiry wanted to see him “sooner rather than later.”

Nvidia shares fall after Huang’s resignation

Nvidia shares fell after the company announced Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO.

After tumbling at the open of trading, Nvidia shares were down 5.3% as of 10:30 a.m. EST Thursday.

The chipmaker became the face of the AI boom under Huang’s leadership. The shares set a record high last month after soaring an astounding 1,722% in four years. But Nvidia’s share price has dropped more than 30% since then, initially on concerns the enthusiasm over AI was overdone and this past week on worries about whether Huang would remain with the company.

The S&P 500 fell 0.4%, and technology stocks were the biggest weights dragging down the benchmark index. Nvidia and several other tech companies have pricey stock values that tend to have more influence on the market’s direction. The tech-heavy Nasdaq fell 0.7%.

___

Trump says his close ally Huang ‘did a fantastic job’

President Donald Trump has reacted to the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang by saying that Huang “has done a fantastic job,” and adding, “There is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple.”

“A Legend replaces a Legend!” Trump wrote on his social media site of Cook, who is Apple’s former CEO.

Huang, who like a lot of top tech CEOs was close with Trump, left his post Thursday after his extramarital affair raised national security concerns. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy.

Late Wednesday, media reports also said Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him. The FBI is investigating Huang’s affair with an alleged Chinese government agent.

___

A ‘watershed’ moment for Nvidia

Huang’s resignation is a watershed moment for Nvidia, said Asa Hiken, senior analyst for research firm eMarketer.

The chipmaker “now has to prove it can maintain its AI dominance without the leader largely responsible for building it,” Hiken said.

“Given the broader AI industry’s heavy dependence on Nvidia’s chips, Huang’s departure introduces uncertainty well beyond the company itself,” he said.

“While Huang’s personal decisions are scandalous, his particular affair with an alleged Chinese spy raises much bigger questions about the security risks facing companies at the center of the AI race,” he said. “AI technology has become critical to U.S. national security, making even the personal relationships of industry leaders a potential vulnerability.”

___

Ripping off ‘the band-aid’

Dan Ives, a technology analyst with the investment firm Yorkville Ives, said removing Jensen was a necessary step by the board of chipmaker Nvidia.

“The old Jensen, the black leather jacket, the Godfather of AI, the rock star viewed as the face of the AI boom, is over and in the past,” he wrote in a note to investors. “His value to the company pre- and post-this week is dramatically different, and the board did what we said it needed to do, which is rip off the band-aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him after this dark moment for Jensen and Nvidia.”

He still recommends investors buy Nvidia stock. He said Nvidia is still two to three years ahead of its nearest competitor and the “demand trajectory” for its chips isn’t changing because Jensen is gone.

___

Singapore says it has barred Alice Huang from returning to the country

Singapore authorities said Thursday that they banned Alice Huang from returning to the country after opening an investigation into Megaspeed over “suspected false declarations” about server purchases.

Investigators looked into whether servers were bought and exported through Singapore to neighboring Malaysia, and then routed to a final destination, contrary to what was declared in Singapore.

Police in the Southeast Asian city-state investigated Alice Huang for “suspected involvement in the possible offences,” but not for espionage, according to a detailed statement issued by the Home Affairs Department.

They seized her passport as part of investigation but returned it in February after concluding that “there was insufficient evidence” that she committed any offences.

But authorities gave her “a stern warning” and barred her from reentering the country because they suspected she “provided information which she knew to be inaccurate” to downplay her role at Megaspeed.

While the statement did not mention China or Nvidia, it said Singapore “does not condone companies using their association with Singapore to circumvent or violate other countries’ export controls through fraud or dishonest practices.”

___

A plunge for Nvidia’s stock drags Wall Street lower

A plunge for Nvidia’s stock is pulling the U.S. market lower, threatening to upend the AI boom that has carried Wall Street to record after record in recent years.

The S&P 500 fell 0.7% Thursday. The weakness in AI stocks sent the Nasdaq composite down 1.5%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average added 127 points. Nvidia tumbled 14% after Jensen Huang, its co-founder and face of the brand, resigned as CEO. Other stocks in the AI industry also fell, though some of Nvidia’s rival chip companies rose. Oil prices swung after President Donald Trump said he’s no longer interested in a deal with Iran.

___

Megaspeed says it is committed to working with the US government

Megaspeed, the Singapore-headquartered data center company at the center of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s scandal, pledged Thursday to cooperate with investigations into potential risks to U.S. national security.

“Megaspeed is committed to working constructively and transparently with the U.S. government,” said the statement signed by its chairman and CEO, Tan Yong Pong, who also goes by James Tan.

Nvidia has said it had “no reason to believe” that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, but that its inquiry would examine all available information.

Megaspeed faced claims last year that it was illicitly shipping advanced Nvidia computer chips into China, but in December said there was “no evidence” of such exports. Singapore has also said it is investigating such allegations.

China has denied that it engaged in an attempt to ensnare Huang, who heads one of the world’s most valuable companies. Nvidia has become a leader in making chips that power AI and Huang has lobbied Washington to loosen limits on sales of Nvidia chips to China. In January, he won Trump’s approval to sell its H200 chips to China.

___

Who is Alice Huang? The woman at the center of Nvidia’s scandal remains elusive

The explosive tale of Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang — involving marital betrayal, international intrigue and accusations of espionage — has rocked the tech and political worlds. Yet basic questions about her life — and how she grew close to one of the world’s most powerful technology executives — remain unanswered.

Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, drew wide attention last month, when The New York Times reported she had formed a close relationship with Nvidia’s chief and passed information to Beijing. U.S. officials, the Times reported, had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese spy who had been recruited to influence California-based Nvidia to make its most advanced chips more available in China, a discovery the paper said set off alarms as high as the White House.

It remains unclear when the apparent affair started and when it might have ended. The Associated Press was unable to reach Alice Huang for comment.

___

Who is Colette Kress?

Nvidia’s interim CEO is Colette Kress, who first joined the chipmaker back in 2013. She’s most recently served as the company’s executive vice president and CFO.

Prior to joining Nvidia, Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments in a variety of roles, according to her executive bio on the company’s website.

In a statement Thursday, Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she was “committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”

___

Shares of Nvidia, one of the largest companies in the world, plunged 10% in premarket trading

The company’s stock has been under pressure for weeks, both because of reporting about the affair and questions about a potential bubble in the AI sector.

Shares slid more than 7% to $160.85 before the opening bell, 34% below the company’s all-time high reached just over a month ago.

The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang had a second affair with an Nvidia executive who reports to him, and analysts said that may force the board to oust him.

ตาก.title: Care gaps hold back Thai women’s employment
ตาก.summary:
Thailand’s strong gains in girls’ education and maternal health have yet to translate into equal economic opportunities, political leadership or personal safety for women, according to the Thailand Country Gender Equality Profile 2026 launched by the United Nations at the Sustainability Expo 2026 (SX2026) in Bangkok.
Produced jointly by the UN in Thailand, UN Women and the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA) in partnership with the Ministry of Social Development and Human Security (MSDHS), the report highlights a stark disconnect between educational attainment and workforce participation. While women outpace men in tertiary education enrollment at 51.6 per cent compared to 38.6 per cent, female labour force participation remains stagnant at 58.9 per cent, lagging well behind men’s 74.7 per cent.

Unpaid care work is identified as the primary barrier holding women back. Among working-age women outside the labour market, 87.3 per cent cite unpaid domestic and caregiving responsibilities as the reason, compared with just 16.3 per cent of men. Gaps in affordable childcare for children under three and insufficient elder care services continue to constrain women’s career choices as Thailand transitions into a super-aged society.
“Thailand’s achievements in girls’ education and women’s health show what sustained investment in public services can deliver,” said UN Resident Coordinator Michaela Friberg-Storey. “The next step is to ensure that these gains translate into equal opportunities to earn a living, lead and live free from violence. That requires tackling the barriers women face at home, at work and in public life.”

Gender-based violence and underrepresentation in decision-making also remain pressing concerns. The report notes that 32.9 per cent of ever-partnered women aged 15–49 have experienced physical or sexual intimate partner violence in their lifetime, with 14.3 per cent experiencing it within the past year. Meanwhile, following the February 2026 elections, women hold 19.8 per cent of seats in the House of Representatives and 22.5 per cent in the Senate—still short of national representation targets.
United Nations Assistant Secretary-General and UN Women Deputy Executive Director Nyaradzayi Gumbonzvanda stressed that data-driven action is essential to reach marginalised groups, including rural women, migrant workers, LGBTQI+ individuals and women with disabilities. “This profile provides a shared evidence base for action. By using its findings to guide policies, budgets and services, we can address persistent inequalities and ensure that progress reaches women and girls who face the greatest barriers,” she said.
During a panel discussion on women’s economic empowerment moderated by UN Women Goodwill Ambassador Cindy Sirinya Bishop, representatives from the public and private sectors outlined concrete steps to address the care burden and expand opportunities.

Representing the MSDHS’s Department of Women’s Affairs and Family Development, specialist Urupin Singhanoi said the ministry is advancing gender-responsive budgeting alongside a proposed family leave policy that would allow men to take leave for caregiving duties. From the private sector, CLP Axtra Plx. Chief Sustainability and Corporate Communications Officer Siriporn Dechsingha noted that women own 51 per cent of the retailer’s supplier network, with a target to reach 60 per cent. To help female farmers and entrepreneurs overcome travel and caregiving constraints, the company launched an online sourcing portal and is expanding regional agricultural learning centres across four regions. Internally, CP Axtra provides lactation rooms across its Makro and Lotus’s branches and has opened traditionally male-dominated roles, such as delivery fleet management, to women, who now make up 58 per cent of its executive team.

Meanwhile, Office of Small and Medium Enterprises Promotion (OSMEP) Assistant Director-General Wittawat Lamsam said the agency has established a formal national definition for women-owned enterprises in collaboration with UN Women. The standardised classification will enable financial institutions and state agencies to better track data and direct targeted credit and market access programmes to female entrepreneurs under Thailand’s upcoming five-year SME master plan.

ตาก.title: Do Good, Be Scammed, and Justice for Boom Panadda
ตาก.summary:
Everything happened so abruptly that when I took a bus on Sukhumvit Road earlier this week, the soap ads inside the bus—where “Boom” Panadda Wongphudee is, or was, the brand ambassador for 24 long years—were still lit bright, while Boom herself is being detained after being accused of siphoning a massive amount of public donations made to her foundation, supposedly meant for helping needy people, for personal indulgence instead.
​”What is good, Boom says it’s good” was the advertising catchphrase of the soap brand, which has become a mantra that many Thais, who are exposed to the phrase over the two decades, would instantly recognise. And yet, the soap company has now terminated her contract.
​The fair-weather friends readily ditch her, even though the justice process has just begun. When Boom’s reputation was supposedly “impeccable,” these very fair-weather friends and admirers relished taking selfies with Boom and praising her. Now it’s the opposite. When she was popular, fair-weather friends got instant social media visibility when posting with Boom. Now that she’s infamous, these very people instead get more social media attention by summarily denouncing Boom as a fake “good person.”
​How convenient…
​Guilty until proven innocent, not innocent until proven guilty, is many Thai people’s understanding of justice. ตาก.summary_original:
Everything happened so abruptly that when I took a bus on Sukhumvit Road earlier this week, the soap ads inside the bus—where “Boom” Panadda Wongphudee is, or was, the brand ambassador for 24 long years—were still lit bright, while Boom herself is being detained after being accused of siphoning a massive amount of public donations made to her foundation, supposedly meant for helping needy people, for personal indulgence instead.

​”What is good, Boom says it’s good” was the advertising catchphrase of the soap brand, which has become a mantra that many Thais, who are exposed to the phrase over the two decades, would instantly recognise. And yet, the soap company has now terminated her contract.

​The fair-weather friends readily ditch her, even though the justice process has just begun. When Boom’s reputation was supposedly “impeccable,” these very fair-weather friends and admirers relished taking selfies with Boom and praising her. Now it’s the opposite. When she was popular, fair-weather friends got instant social media visibility when posting with Boom. Now that she’s infamous, these very people instead get more social media attention by summarily denouncing Boom as a fake “good person.”

​How convenient…

​Guilty until proven innocent, not innocent until proven guilty, is many Thai people’s understanding of justice. They are quick to judge, and quick to believe or be scammed — but even quicker to ditch her, now that she is being detained and branded as arguably the biggest Thai scammer of the decade.

​The problematic notion of “good people” that are too good to be true is prevalent in Thailand. Many Thais love idealised or vilified characterisations — it’s either simplistic white or black. Many Thais are fond of public figures who are too good to be true. Boom is not the only such idol.

​People can be too trusting. Prone to fairy tales. No wonder scam victims are plentiful in Thailand.

According to findings released by Thailand’s Economic Crime Suppression Division (ECD) this month regarding Boom’s “Do Good” Foundation (Ongkorn Thamdee), police have not specified the exact number of unique individuals who donated, as many people contributed multiple times. However, investigators tracked over 3.2 million separate donation transfers across three bank accounts totaling over 815 million baht.

The amount allegedly siphoned, according to investigators, is 527 million baht, or approximately 65 per cent of the total donations, diverted for personal benefit rather than charitable work.

​Police reported that the 527 million baht was channelled into 12 categories of non-charitable expenditures. These included 99 million baht transferred directly to her husband, Atip “Got” Anantawan; 36 million baht transferred to foundation committee members; 24 million baht invested in mutual funds; 19 million baht spent on personal credit card bills; and 18 million baht paid to contractors for building a pool villa in Phuket (with additional transfers linked to construction projects in Pathum Thani). Also, 10 million baht spent on life insurance and 4.6 million baht transferred to Panadda’s father.

Then there was 2.7 million baht spent on luxury handbags and jewelry, which was withdrawn from mutual fund accounts.

The bottom line: Only about 280 million baht of the total funds collected was found to have actually been used for legitimate foundation activities.

Khaosod English reports on Wednesday that police revealed approximately 90 per cent of the first batch of 32 designer handbags seized in the investigation appear to be counterfeit, pending official authentication.

On Wednesday, investigators searched two more condominiums registered in Panadda’s name, seizing another 12 designer handbags, 53 pieces of jewellery, 11 scarves, and four items of clothing. Police are now tracing the origins of the luxury goods and the money used to purchase them, while questioning people linked to the foundation’s financial transactions.

​The shockwave through the whole “Do Good” industry is palpable, with the authorities now looking into a dozen other well-known foundations for possible misuse of public donations.

​Henceforth, there needs to be more transparency and accountability. Details of donations made, and how much and how it was spent, should be posted online for all to examine and independently reviewed by a third-party auditor on a monthly basis.
​
Temple donations should also be better regulated, as there are, according to official statistics from the National Office of Buddhism (ONAB), over 44,000 active, registered Buddhist temples, or wat, across the country. Misuse and wasteful use of resources by temples should also be tackled, with fewer concrete structures and more hospices, shelters for the poor, orphans, and elderly, and schools preferred.

​In the end, whatever you think about Boom, she should be regarded as innocent until proven guilty. I am not a fan of Boom and had never donated to her “Do Good” Foundation.

Nevertheless, if Thai society learned a thing or two from this case, then perhaps not all the donated money went to waste — to real or counterfeit luxury bags, and more.

ตาก.title: Chiang Rai Water Security Moves Beyond Emergency Supplies
ตาก.summary:
CHIANG RAI – Provincial water authorities are abandoning reliance on cross-border waterways in northern Thailand, shifting primary municipal intake from the Kok River to the domestic Lao River after heavy metal spikes forced emergency shutoffs across border communities.

The Provincial Waterworks Authority rolled out the multi-phase pivot this week after arsenic contamination in the neighboring Sai River reached 28 times national safety limits, cutting tap water to 14 villages in Mae Sai district and exposing fragile links across Chiang Rai’s homes, hospitals, farms and tourism economy.

• Water engineers are rerouting urban supply from the transboundary Kok River to the domestic Lao River while planning Mekong River diversions for Mae Sai.

• Arsenic levels in the Sai River surged to 28 times Thailand’s 0.01 milligram-per-liter limit during monsoon runoff, forcing water truck deployments for 14 villages.

The crisis stems from geography outside Thailand’s jurisdiction. Both the Kok and Sai rivers originate in Myanmar’s Shan State, where satellite mapping and field investigations by the Shan Human Rights Foundation identified rapidly expanding open-pit gold and rare-earth mining operations near the headwaters.

Heavy rains wash loose mine tailings directly into mountain tributaries. Since severe regional flooding in 2024, residents along the Kok River reported that the waterway stopped clearing during the cool season, turning persistently turbid with heavy metal sediment.

In early August 2026, monthly testing by the Pollution Control Department recorded Sai River arsenic concentrations at 28 times the national drinking threshold of 0.01 milligrams per liter. Although September readings in the Kok, Ruak and Mekong rivers returned within legal limits, Thai Natural Resources and Environment Minister Suchart Chomklin acknowledged on Nov. 10 that restoring contaminated riverbeds remains slow and requires diplomatic intervention with Myanmar.

Conventional municipal treatment plants built to filter river silt cannot reliably strip dissolved arsenic during sudden turbidity spikes. When raw water turns toxic, operators must shut intake valves entirely to protect treatment membranes and public health.

To eliminate that single point of failure, the Provincial Waterworks Authority is executing a three-stage source transition. First, engineers are expanding distribution lines from the Lao River—a tributary originating entirely within Thailand’s Wiang Pa Pao mountains—to supply central Chiang Rai neighborhoods previously dependent on the Kok River.

Second, crews are preparing emergency pipelines to divert Mekong River water toward border communities in Mae Sai, backed by temporary mobile reserve tanks. Third, planners are designing a permanent intake on the Kham River in Mae Chan district alongside a new Chiang Saen waterworks facility to anchor long-term provincial capacity.

Water insecurity hits every layer of the provincial economy differently. Across 14 affected Mae Sai villages and riverside settlements like Ban Ruam Mit, families have abandoned shallow household wells and local river fish, spending hundreds of baht monthly on bottled drinking water after learning that boiling fails to remove heavy metals.

ตาก.title: What’s at stake in the renewed tensions over the Falkland Islands?
ตาก.summary:
A legal battle is under way between Argentina and the United Kingdom, triggered by an oil project off the coast of the disputed Falkland Islands.

The Argentinian government wants to stop drilling in the area by a joint British-Israeli venture, saying it should not take place until the issue of sovereignty has been resolved.

For its part, the British government rejects these arguments, stressing its full sovereignty over the area.

The case is the latest chapter in the dispute between the UK and Argentina.

The two countries went to war in the early 1980s after Argentina invaded the Falklands. So, what are the implications of this case?

Diego Guelar – Former Argentinian ambassador to the United States

Javier Farje – Latin American affairs specialist and historian

Tobias Ellwood – Former British MP who served as a minister at the Ministry of Defence and the UK Foreign Office

ตาก.title: ‘ฉก.ราชมนู’ ร่วมกับ ด่านตรวจพืชแม่สอด จับกระบะขน อะโวคาโดเถื่อน 3.5 ตัน นำเข้าจากเมียนมา
ตาก.summary:
‘ฉก.ราชมนู’ ร่วมกับ ด่านตรวจพืชแม่สอด สกัดจับกุมกระบะขน อะโวคาโดเถื่อน 130 กล่อง น้ำหนัก 3.5 ตัน ลักลอบนำเข้าจากเมียนมา ไม่พบหลักฐานการนำเข้าสินค้าอย่างถูกกฎหมาย
วันที่ 13 พ.ย.2569 หน่วยเฉพาะกิจราชมนู (ฉก.ราชมนู) บูรณาการกำลังร่วมกับหน่วยงานที่เกี่ยวข้อง สกัดกั้นการลักลอบนำเข้าสินค้าผิดกฎหมายตามแนวชายแดนไทย–เมียนมา ล่าสุดตรวจพบรถกระบะต้องสงสัยบรรทุกอะโวคาโดเต็มคันรถ จำนวน 130 กล่อง น้ำหนักรวมประมาณ 3,500 กิโลกรัม โดยไม่มีเอกสารการนำเข้า ก่อนจับกุมผู้ขับขี่และนำของกลางส่งพนักงานสอบสวนดำเนินคดีตามกฎหมาย

โดยหน่วยเฉพาะกิจราชมนู โดยกองร้อยทหารราบที่ 1431 จัดกำลังพลบูรณาการร่วมกับเจ้าหน้าที่ชุดศูนย์อำนวยการร่วมพิทักษ์ความมั่นคงทางการเกษตรและอาหาร พระพิรุณ (ศพร.) และเจ้าหน้าที่ด่านตรวจพืชแม่สอด ลงพื้นที่ปฏิบัติการสกัดกั้นการลักลอบขนสินค้าผิดกฎหมาย บริเวณถนนสายท่าอาจ–วังตะเคียน อำเภอแม่สอด จังหวัดตาก

ระหว่างปฏิบัติหน้าที่ เจ้าหน้าที่พบรถกระบะคอกสูงต้องสงสัย อีซูซุ ดีแม็กซ์ บรรทุกสินค้ามาเต็มคันรถ จึงเข้าตรวจสอบโดยแสดงตัวเป็นเจ้าหน้าที่ ก่อนดำเนินการตรวจค้นรถคันดังกล่าวอย่างละเอียด ตรวจพบอะโวคาโดจำนวน 130 กล่อง น้ำหนักรวมประมาณ 3,500 กิโลกรัม โดยสินค้าดังกล่าวนำเข้าจากประเทศเมียนมา โดยไม่พบเอกสารหลักฐานการนำเข้าสินค้าอย่างถูกต้องตามกฎหมาย

เจ้าหน้าที่จึงร่วมกันจับกุมผู้ขับขี่รถกระบะในข้อกล่าวหากระทำความผิดตามพระราชบัญญัติกักพืช พ.ศ. 2507 และพระราชบัญญัติศุลกากร พ.ศ. 2560 พร้อมตรวจยึดสินค้าอะโวคาโดทั้งหมดเป็นของกลาง ก่อนนำส่งพนักงานสอบสวนสภ.แม่สอด เพื่อดำเนินการตามกฎหมายต่อไป
‘ฉก.ราชมนู’ ร่วมกับ ด่านตรวจพืชแม่สอด จับกระบะขน อะโวคาโดเถื่อน 3.5 ตัน นำเข้าจากเมียนมา

ตาก.summary:
WELLINGTON, New Zealand (AP) — Nauru’s president, David Adeang , has said all opposition lawmakers in parliament have joined his government, a move he said reflected “unity, stability and shared purpose” in the Pacific Island country’s politics.
The unusual move leaves the 19-member parliament without any political opposition. While it’s common for island countries in the South Pacific Ocean to take fluid approaches to forming government and opposition blocs or for lawmakers to switch between them, political debate is habitually robust and Nauru is rare in having no opposing politicians at all.
In a Facebook post Tuesday, Adeang didn’t explain what had prompted the change beyond a “shared commitment” to put Nauru’s interests first. He also didn’t suggest who would supply the scrutiny usually provided by opponents in a country with a single house of parliament.
“There will still be a diversity of views and robust debate as in any strong and healthy democracy,” Adeang wrote.
No political opposition is a first for Nauru
The appointment of two lawmakers, Pyon Deiye and Jason Bingham Agir, as deputy cabinet ministers meant that Nauru’s parliament was in total support of the government for the first time since the country’s independence in 1968, Adeang said.
Government Facebook posts announcing the change were the sole source of information about it; all news outlets in the country of 12,000 people are government-owned. Foreign reporters are discouraged from traveling there, with journalist visa applications priced at 8,000 Australian dollars ($5,445).
Adeang made global news headlines in August when he said his country would officially become known as Naoero , making it the latest state to formally adopt the local spelling of its name. It brought international attention to a country visited by few.

Adeang made global news headlines in August when he said his country would officially become known as Naoero, making it the latest state to formally adopt the local spelling of its name. It brought international attention to a country visited by few.

Power competition in the Pacific Islands has directed keener attention to local politics

Nauru, a constitutional republic and United Nations member, is one of the world’s smallest countries by both population and size. Limited infrastructure, a remote location and the environmental damage wrought by phosphate mining mean it attracts few visitors, unlike many other Pacific islands where foreign tourism is the main economic driver.

But it’s among the South Pacific countries where domestic politics have drawn keener outside interest in recent years as the sprawling ocean where Nauru is located has become the site of geopolitical contest between major powers.

The potentially wealthy exclusive economic zones surrounding some of the poorest Pacific nations and the strategic importance of their locations in times of global volatility have provoked a race between China and Western countries with interests in the region to win influence with governments there.

Nauru is no exception. In 2024, it was one of a dwindling number of countries to hold diplomatic relations with Taipei, but severed them in order to resume ties with Beijing, which holds that Taiwan is part of China. It’s become one of Beijing’s warmest allies in the region since.

Australia in turn signed a lucrative pact with Adeang later in 2024 in which Nauru promised Canberra veto power over any security deals with Beijing.

The newest members of Adeang’s government have traveled with him to China

Adeang’s government said Friday that the president had arrived in China for meetings with officials, accompanied by other lawmakers including newly appointed cabinet members Deiye and Agir.

The president has led the country since 2023 when a no-confidence motion ousted his predecessor. He was chosen unopposed to continue in the job among lawmakers sworn in after the 2025 election.

In 2014, then Justice Minister Adeang suspended opposition lawmakers from Parliament for remarks they made to international news outlets. Most lawmakers in Nauru run as independents and don’t belong to political parties, which is common in Pacific Island countries.

Freedom House, a Washington-based organization that promotes democracy, said in its 2026 report that Nauru’s people “generally enjoy political rights and civil liberties” but that corruption was “an ongoing challenge.” The country was one of the world’s richest per capita at the height of phosphate exports but the economy plummeted when the industry collapsed.

Nauru experimented with a golden passport scheme and became a tax haven for a period. It now subsists on foreign aid, sales of tuna fisheries licenses in its waters and funding from Australia first to host that country’s offshore detention facilities for asylum seekers and later to accommodate foreign criminals Australia wanted to deport.

ตาก.title: Chiang Mai Airport gears up for Yi Peng Festival with 35,000 passengers expected daily
ตาก.summary:
Chiang Mai International Airport is preparing to welcome tourists for the 2026 Yi Peng Festival, with passenger numbers expected to reach 35,000 per day. The airport is arranging staff and resources to handle the expected increase in travelers to
provide convenient and efficient services.
On 10 November 2026, Chiang Mai Governor Thotsaphon Phuean Udom chaired a meeting
to discuss preparations for the 2026 Yi Peng Festival.
Yi Peng is a traditional festival in northern Thailand. The festival features the release of sky
lanterns into the night sky, fireworks displays, and colourful lanterns decorating temples and homes. These activities reflect Lanna culture, beliefs, and traditions. Visitors can also
experience traditional activities and local celebrations that showcase the unique charm of
northern Thailand.

Yi Peng is observed in northern Thailand, particularly Chiang Mai, on the full moon of the 12th lunar month — the same day as Loy Krathong. While Yi Peng is marked by the release of lanterns into the sky, Loy Krathong sees people float decorated baskets on rivers and waterways.
This year, the Yi Peng Festival takes place between 24 and 25 November.
Due to aviation safety measures, the airport’s operating hours will be reduced from 20 to
approximately 12 hours per day, while daily flights are expected to increase from 210 to as
many as 232, potentially concentrating passenger traffic during peak periods.
To accommodate more than 32,000 passengers per day, a number that could lead to
overcrowding in the passenger terminals, Chiang Mai International Airport is increasing
staffing and resources, adjusting check-in counters and adding security screening points to
ensure smooth passenger flow.

The airport will also temporarily install two additional X-ray baggage screening machines,
following the aviation security standards and requirements set by the Civil Aviation
Authority of Thailand (CAAT). Staff will also be assigned to assist passengers at various
service points to improve service efficiency and reduce waiting times.
In addition, passengers are encouraged to use self-service systems, including Online
Check-in, Self Check-in kiosks (CUSS), and Self Bag Drop systems, with staff available to
guide and assist passengers in using these services.

Getting around Chiang Mai during the festival should be relatively straightforward, with several transport options available at the airport, including airport taxis, limousines, shuttle buses and RTC City Buses . Ride-hailing services such as Grab will also be available, alongside car rental services.
With large crowds expected at popular festival venues, travellers should plan their journeys ahead of time and allow extra time for traffic and possible delays, particularly when travelling by taxi or public transport.

Beyond the city centre, visitors can also explore Yi Peng celebrations and cultural events in other parts of Chiang Mai province, including Mae On district. These offer an opportunity to experience local traditions away from some of the better-known festival locations.
